cover.headline: India's forging leader with a real defence option, priced as if the option has already paid
cover.lead: Bharat Forge is India's largest forging company (standalone EBITDA margin 27.5% in FY26) with a fast-growing defence arm (KSSL, order book ₹11,196 cr) and loss-making plants in Europe and the US. Consolidated EPS was flat for seven years (₹22.2 in FY19, ₹22.6 in FY26). We expect it to roughly double by FY28E as defence deliveries start, the German steel plant (CDP) closes and US trucks recover: EPS before exceptional items of ₹29.7 / ₹41.8 / ₹52.5 for FY27-29E on the post-QIP share count, ~10% below the street. The street values the stock on **P/E on FY28E (35-40x)**. The stock's own forward P/E median since 2021 is 48.0x on clean EPS; cut by the 7.8% auto-component de-rating that gives **44x Sep-28E EPS of ₹47.1 = {{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}}): we initiate with HOLD.** Cross-checks: EV/EBITDA ₹1,684, DCF ₹638. Bull case {{scen.bull.tp|inr}}; bear case {{scen.bear.tp|inr}}.

arguments.h: The Indian forging core is good and recovering
arguments.p: Standalone revenue fell 5% in FY26 on the US truck destocking but held a 27.5% margin; Q1FY27 revenue rose 11.5% with exports +12%. Management guides 20-25% growth for the Indian manufacturing business in FY27 (H2-weighted) and is adding ~₹1,800 cr of capacity for large engines, aerospace and semiconductor parts, funded by a ₹2,000 cr QIP (Sep-2026).

KSSL's revenue was ₹1,422-1,567 cr for three years while the order book grew to ₹11,196 cr; Q1FY27 revenue rose 71% with a 17% margin. ATAGS and carbine deliveries wait for approvals. We model +35% / +35% / +20% and margins of 15-18%, below management's 22-23% target.

arguments.h: Overseas: the drag should shrink, not disappear
arguments.p: Europe and the US earned a 3.8% EBITDA margin on ₹5,398 cr in FY26 and lost ₹328 cr before tax. CDP (₹1,595 cr revenue) will be wound down by end-CY2027 after a ₹358 cr charge in Q1FY27. We give credit for the exit and a partial US recovery; group EBITDA margin {{F.ebitdaMargin.0|pct}} / {{F.ebitdaMargin.1|pct}} / {{F.ebitdaMargin.2|pct}}.

arguments.h: Valuation: the defence story is in the price
arguments.p: At ₹1,926 the stock trades at 40.9x our Sep-28E EPS and ~94x trailing; the DCF supports only ₹638. Our 44x comes from its own history; the street's median target is ₹2,183 (+13%). At the street's EPS our multiple would give ~₹2,320: the gap to the street is as much earnings as multiple.

catalysts: Q2FY27 results (due by mid-November 2026): margin recovery after the Q1 cost hit, US plant restart, KSSL execution.
ATAGS final production approval (FOPM) and first deliveries; CQB carbine serial production in H2FY27.
North American Class 8 orders and production into calendar 2027; US tariff decisions on aluminium.
CDP wind-down milestones (closure targeted for Q3 CY2027) and use of the ₹2,000 cr QIP (capex, Indian M&A).
New defence orders (naval systems, ammunition, energetics plant licence in Andhra Pradesh).

sections.title: Five businesses: Indian forgings earn the money; defence is the growth story; overseas is the drag

blocks.p: Bharat Forge, the flagship of Pune's Kalyani Group, is India's largest forging company. It hammers and presses steel (and aluminium) into safety-critical parts - crankshafts, connecting rods, front axle beams, steering knuckles - and machines them. Trucks and cars still make up most of the demand, in India and abroad (the US truck makers are its largest export customers), but a growing share is "industrial": oil and gas, construction and mining, rail, marine, large engines for data-centre and power-generation sets, aerospace and semiconductor equipment. Since FY24 it also has a real defence business, run through the wholly owned **Kalyani Strategic Systems (KSSL)**: towed and mounted artillery (ATAGS), protected vehicles, CQB carbines, shells and, since Q1FY27, naval gas-turbine generator sets.

sections.title: Sixty years of forging; a decade of overseas losses; now a pivot to India, defence and aerospace

blocks.p: Founded in 1961 and led by Chairman and MD B.N. Kalyani (with Amit Kalyani as Vice-Chairman and Joint MD), Bharat Forge grew into a global truck-parts supplier in the 2000s by buying forging plants in Germany and Sweden and later building aluminium forging in Germany and the US. Those plants have rarely made money. The last five years have been a pivot back to India: a defence business built from scratch (artillery, vehicles, small arms), castings (JS Autocast, 2022), axles (K Drive, 2025), aerospace and large-engine parts, while e-mobility was written off and the German steel plant is being closed.

blocks.callout: **Read the history with care:** reported EPS swings with exceptional items in both directions (+₹205 cr in FY22; −₹154-157 cr in FY25 and FY26; −₹358 cr in Q1FY27), so we value the company on EPS before exceptional items and compute its own multiple history on the same basis (valuation chapter).

sections.title: Three end-markets: the US truck cycle, Indian vehicles, and a defence and power-gen capex boom

blocks.p: Bharat Forge sells into three very different cycles. **North American trucks** (its largest export market) went through a destocking slump in FY26: standalone exports fell 15% and Americas exports from ₹3,317 cr to ₹2,487 cr. The cycle turned in Q4FY26; truck makers guide calendar 2026 roughly flat to up (table). **Indian vehicles** got a lift from the Sep-2025 GST cut; India's auto-component industry reached US$85.9 bn in FY26. **Defence and industrial capex**: India's defence production was ₹1.78 tn in FY26 with 24% from private firms; the Navy plans ~140 new ships; data-centre build-outs need standby power-gen engines, whose crankshafts and other forgings Bharat Forge supplies.

bullets: **Tariffs.** US tariffs and North American truck destocking cut standalone exports 15% in FY26 (Americas exports ₹3,317 cr to ₹2,487 cr). An India-US trade deal in early 2026 removed the punitive 25% duty (management, Feb-2026). US tariff on raw aluminium is 50% (Canadian supply), hurting BF's US aluminium plants.

**Energy and labour (2026).** The Iran war and LPG crisis (Q1FY27) raised energy and logistics costs (~160bp on standalone margin) and sent contract labour home (manpower 70-75% of normal in Aug-2026).
**Europe.** Management calls Europe "a secular problem" (Feb-2026): high energy costs, weak demand and 60-65% plant utilisation. That is why CDP is closing and some of its work is moving to India.

blocks.callout: **Verdict:** the defence tailwind is real and Bharat Forge is one of its few private beneficiaries with its own artillery designs. But it shows up in orders far faster than in revenue: KSSL grew −0% in FY26 while the order book rose from ~₹9,400 cr to ₹10,961 cr. We model defence revenue +35% a year for two years; management's 22-23% margin target would need a doubling of KSSL's FY26 margin.

sections.title: Standalone forgings: a 27% margin business coming out of a US truck downturn

blocks.p: Standalone revenue fell 5% in FY26 to ₹8,396 cr as exports dropped 15% (North American truck destocking, tariffs), while domestic sales rose 6.5%. Tonnage fell 8.5% to 2.38 lakh tonnes. The margin held at 27.5%. Q1FY27 was the second quarter of recovery: revenue ₹2,347 cr (+11.5%), exports +12% (Americas +15.0%), tonnage +8%, but EBITDA margin 26.2% after ~160bp of energy and input costs not yet passed on.

blocks.callout: **Our view:** the business is sound - few companies can make a 30-tonne crankshaft and a 0.2 kg aerospace part in one group - but it is a supplier to cyclical customers. Our +15-16% growth already assumes the US truck recovery, aerospace doubling and CDP work moving to India; the margin returns to ~27.5%, not the 28.5% of FY25.

sections.title: Defence: a ₹11,196 cr order book, but revenue was flat for three years and margins were thin

blocks.p: KSSL's revenue jumped to ₹1,422 cr in FY24 on artillery-shell exports and then stalled (₹1,567 cr in FY25, ₹1,562 cr in FY26). Margins were 4.7%, 6.3% and 10.1%. Q1FY27 was the best quarter yet: ₹423 cr revenue (+71%) and a 17.2% margin. The order book rose to ₹11,196 cr (Jun-26), with ₹681 cr won in Q1 including 12 naval gas-turbine generator sets. The next steps are deliveries of ATAGS (towed artillery, co-developed with DRDO) and CQB carbines from the new defence plant, which wait for a final production approval (FOPM).

blocks.callout: **Our view:** this is a real defence franchise with its own designs (10 artillery platforms developed), and India's procurement is shifting to private firms. But the order book is government-paced: approvals slip, deliveries are lumpy, and margins have averaged ~7% over FY24-FY26 against a 22-23% target. We model ₹3,417 cr of revenue in FY29E at 18%; even then KSSL is ~12% of group EBITDA.

sections.title: Overseas: ₹5,400 cr of revenue earning ~4%; CDP closing; India subsidiaries growing at thin margins

blocks.p: The European plants earned EBITDA of ₹151 cr on ₹3,865 cr in FY26 (3.9%) and lost ₹195 cr before tax; the US plants ₹54 cr on ₹1,534 cr and lost ₹133 cr. In Q1FY27 Europe made 2.8% and the US −0.8% (presses down). CDP Bharat Forge (₹1,595 cr revenue, ~41% of Europe) will be wound down and liquidated by end-CY2027; ₹358 cr was provided in Q1FY27. In India, K Drive (axles, 3-5% margin) and JS Autocast (castings, 11-14%) grow fast but earn far less than the forging business.

blocks.callout: **Honest verdict:** Bharat Forge has a narrow but genuine moat in India: scale, metallurgy and decades of qualification with global truck and engine makers. It has no pricing power over those customers, and no advantage in its European and US plants. Defence could become a second moat - own artillery designs are rare - but the evidence so far is orders, not profits.

sections.title: A decade of cycles: revenue 2.2x since FY16, EPS barely higher than in FY19

blocks.p: Consolidated revenue went from ₹6,809 cr in FY16 to ₹16,812 cr in FY26 (9.5% a year), but profit did not follow. EPS was ₹22.17 in FY19 and ₹22.58 in FY26: seven years with no net earnings growth. Three things ate the growth: (1) the overseas plants (Germany, Sweden, the US aluminium plants) added revenue but earned EBITDA margins of 0-4% and lost ₹330-470 cr a year before tax in FY24-FY26; (2) the e-mobility venture lost ₹67-138 cr a year at EBITDA before being written down; (3) exceptional charges in most years. The Indian forging business did well throughout: standalone EBITDA margins of 25-29%.

blocks.callout: **Our view:** Bharat Forge is two companies in one set of accounts. The Indian business (standalone forgings, defence, castings, axles) earned ₹2,758 cr of EBITDA on ₹11,308 cr of revenue in FY26 (24.4%). The overseas and e-mobility units earned ₹163 cr on ₹5,503 cr and lost ₹380 cr before tax (before exchange differences and exceptional items). The investment case is that the first keeps growing and the second stops losing money; the history says the second has repeatedly disappointed.

bullets: Standalone margin 26.2% bore ~160bp of energy, input and logistics cost increases (Iran war, LPG crisis); ~28% normalised. Recoveries are being negotiated and will lift revenue and cost together, so the margin improves gradually (CFO, Kedar Dixit).

CDP Bharat Forge (German steel forging) restructuring on track: closure by Q3 CY2027; a ~EUR30 mn (~₹330 cr) manpower-redundancy provision taken in Q1, paid out over 6-12 months; part of CDP's orders move to India.

US steel forging had ~3 months without production after press breakdowns (EBITDA -₹4 cr); fixed, recovery in Q2. Target margins ~12% (steel) and 15-16% (aluminium) "hopefully next year", but the 50% US tariff on Canadian aluminium is the obstacle.

Defence: largest naval order so far (12 marine gas-turbine generator sets for the Navy); new defence facility enters serial production this year for ATAGS and CQB carbines; ATAGS start waits for FOPM approval ("a few weeks of delay"). Steady-state defence EBITDA margin target 22-23%.
Aerospace ~₹400 cr, to double in ~2 years (Baramati ring mill from Q4FY27); semiconductor components USD30-40 mn in 2 years; energy/data-centre business to double in four years.

Board approved a fund raise of up to ₹2,500 cr for ~₹1,800 cr of growth capex over 12-18 months (forging, ring rolling, machining; energetics plant in Andhra Pradesh) and possible Indian M&A; asset turn above 1.5x. Manpower back to 70-75% of normal.
Outlook: FY27 growth of 20-25% for the India manufacturing business, more pronounced in H2; FY28 "should also be a strong year".

blocks.callout: **Track record:** management guides with confidence and the timing often slips: overseas recoveries were promised for years, ATAGS deliveries have moved from FY26 to H2FY27, and the 25% FY27 India growth guide became 20-25% in August. We haircut the guidance rather than reject it: our India manufacturing growth for FY27E is ~20% (low end).

sections.title: Capital-hungry: working capital ~28% of revenue, two QIPs in two years, ROCE stuck at 12-13%

blocks.p: Bharat Forge needs a lot of capital to grow. Inventories run at ~195 days and receivables ~85 days (FY26, Screener basis), so working capital is ~28% of revenue; every ₹1,000 cr of growth ties up ~₹280 cr of cash. Over FY21-FY26 the group generated ₹7,767 cr of operating cash flow and spent ₹8,073 cr on capex and acquisitions; free cash flow after dividends was negative and the gap was filled with debt and equity (₹1,650 cr QIP in Dec-2024, ₹2,000 cr QIP in Sep-2026). ROCE has been 8-13% since FY22, at or below the cost of capital.

blocks.callout: **The capital question:** management is now spending ~₹1,800 cr of growth capex in 12-18 months and looking at Indian acquisitions, funded by the new QIP. The Indian bolt-ons have worked (JS Autocast was valued at 3.5-4x its cost when Premji Invest bought 23%); the overseas and EV bets did not. We would like to see the CDP exit lift group ROCE before more capital goes in.

sections.title: Earnings quality: clean audits, but recurring "exceptional" charges, no tax shield on losses and weak cash conversion

bullets: **"Exceptional" items recur.** ₹12 cr in FY24, ₹157 cr in FY25, ₹154 cr in FY26 and ₹358 cr in Q1FY27 (e-mobility write-downs, labour codes, CDP closure). Investors who use "adjusted" EPS should remember the charges are real cash or capital losses. Our FY27E reported EPS (₹22.4) includes the Q1 charge; before it, ₹29.7.

**Tax.** The group pays 35-37% of reported PBT because overseas and e-mobility losses earn no tax credit (India pays ~25%). We model 36% / 28% / 27%; our check gives ~25.5-26% on profit excluding the loss-making units every year.
**Cash conversion is weak.** Operating cash flow was ₹1,487 cr in FY26 on EBITDA of ₹2,917 cr (51%), as receivables rose ₹709 cr. Working capital is ~28% of revenue; inventories ~195 days.

**Hedge losses in OCI.** USD329 mn and EUR95 mn of forward contracts hedge export sales; a ₹457 cr unrealised hedge loss sat in other comprehensive income at Mar-2026 and flows into revenue as the contracts mature.

**Related-party steel.** Bharat Forge buys special steel from promoter-group Kalyani Steels and Saarloha Advanced Materials (approved limits ₹1,800 cr and ₹3,450 cr a year). Prices are declared at arm's length; it is still a large flow to entities the family owns more of.
**Segment disclosure.** Useful management tables (standalone, KSSL, K Drive, castings, Europe, US) but no CDP-only profit figure and no order-book breakdown by programme.

blocks.callout: **Accounting flag: AMBER.** Unqualified audit by B S R & Co. (KPMG network), no aggressive capitalisation visible; the amber is for recurring exceptional charges, weak cash conversion and large related-party steel purchases.

sections.title: Net debt ~₹3,900-4,300 cr (0.4x equity), mostly working-capital lines; AA+ rated

blocks.p: At Jun-2026 the group had ₹2,152 cr of long-term debt and ₹4,845 cr of working-capital loans and bill discounting against ₹2,730 cr of cash and liquid investments: net debt ~₹4,267 cr, 0.45x equity and 1.4x EBITDA. Standalone Bharat Forge is almost net cash (0.18x). Since then the QIP has added ~₹2,000 cr of cash (Sep-2026), which the engine does not show (it starts from the Mar-2026 balance sheet). ICRA and CARE rate the company AA+ (Stable); ICRA reaffirmed on 22-Sep-2026.

sections.title: Ownership: the Kalyani family at 44%, Indian funds 32%, foreign funds 15%

blocks.p: The Kalyani family owns 44.07% (Jun-2026), almost all through investment companies (Kalyani Investment, Sundaram Trading, KSL Holdings, BF Investment, Ajinkya Investment), with nothing pledged. Mutual funds own 20.74%, insurers 7.67%, the NPS (SBI pension fund) 3.48%, foreign portfolio investors 15.04% and retail ~8.54%; 2,32,361 shareholders. The Sep-2026 QIP (1.06 cr shares) diluted promoters to ~43.1% (44.07% x 47.81 / 48.87); the Sep-2026 filing itself was published in October, after our as-of date.

blocks.callout: Our FY28E EPS (₹41.8) is ~10% below the street even after adjusting the street for the QIP dilution. The gap: lower group revenue (we take CDP's ~₹1,600 cr out of Europe), defence margins of 17% rather than 20%+, and a slower US recovery. Our view is that the earnings will roughly double from FY26, but the street is already there.

sections.title: The street: split between Buy and Hold, targets ₹1,931-2,400, median ₹2,183

blocks.p: Six houses published after the Q1FY27 results (10-11 Aug-2026): Emkay Buy ₹2,400, ICICI Securities Buy ₹2,400, Nomura Neutral ₹2,260, CLSA Hold ₹2,106, InCred Hold ₹2,103 and Motilal Oswal Neutral ₹1,931: median ₹2,183, +13% from the 30-Sep-2026 close of ₹1,926. Earlier notes still standing: ICICI Direct Buy ₹2,360 (Jun), Geojit Sell ₹1,732 (May), Axis Direct Buy ₹2,095 (Apr). The houses that disclose a method mostly use consolidated P/E on FY28E (MOSL 40x; ICICI Securities 35x in May-2026); Emkay uses 23x Jun-28E EV/EBITDA. None disclosed a sum of the parts with defence valued separately in the notes we could read. Bulls focus on defence and aerospace; the holds on valuation and the overseas drag.

exhibit.title: Critiques we take seriously
head: Argument
Who
rows: At ~94x trailing and ~41x our Sep-28E EPS the stock already prices defence and aerospace success; the DCF does not get close to the price.
Defence revenue was flat for three years (FY24-FY26 ~₹1,420-1,570 cr) while the order book doubled: execution, not orders, is the issue.
Overseas operations have destroyed value for a decade (EBITDA ~1-4%, PBT losses of ₹330-470 cr a year); the CDP closure costs ~₹358 cr and removes ~₹1,600 cr of revenue.
GAM Research; Citi and Goldman questions on the Aug-2026 call
Two equity raises in two years (₹1,650 cr in Dec-2024, ₹2,000 cr in Sep-2026) despite a "strong balance sheet": shareholders fund growth and M&A.
Exports depend on the North American truck cycle and US tariff policy (Americas exports -25% in FY26).
Bulls: defence order book 7x KSSL revenue, aerospace doubling, data-centre engines, CDP losses ending: EPS can double by FY28.

sections.title: Our honest summary: a good Indian business and a real defence option, fully priced; HOLD at 40.9x Sep-28E

blocks.callout: **What you are buying:** India's largest forger with a 27% margin core, a defence arm with a ₹11,196 cr order book and its own artillery designs, a growing aerospace and power-gen business, and an overseas drag that should shrink as the German steel plant closes by end-2027.

**What you are paying:** 46.1x our FY28E and 40.9x Sep-28E EPS, after seven years of flat EPS (FY19-FY26). Our EPS roughly doubles by FY28E and we are still ~10% below the street. The stock's own forward P/E median since 2021 is 48.0x on clean EPS; auto-component stocks were below their five-year medians on 30-Sep-2026. That gives 44x and {{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}}): HOLD.

bullets: **Rating: HOLD, target {{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}}).** Our ratings follow the upside to our 12−month target: BUY at +15% or more, HOLD between −5% and +15%, SELL below −5%.
**We would turn BUY below ~₹1,800** and SELL above ~₹2,180 on today's numbers, or earlier if defence deliveries start on time and overseas losses visibly shrink in H2FY27.
**This is mostly a valuation call.** The street median target is ₹2,183; our EPS is lower, and our multiple is derived from the stock's own history rather than from the defence theme.
**Biggest swing factor:** each 1x of P/E is ~₹47 a share; each 1pp of standalone EBITDA margin is ~₹112 cr of FY28E EBITDA, ~₹73 a share at our multiple.
